name: Handles & Knobs
tagline: The one detail every client actually touches
description: Handles are jewellery on joinery: the cheapest way to lift a scheme and the fastest way to date it. This section runs from concealed profiles for handle-less kitchens through to leather and solid brass pieces for statement furniture.

materials.name: Cabinet handle (D / bar)
materials.blurb: The standard pull, from 96 mm to 1200 mm centres
materials.description: A straightforward bar or D-pull in stainless, aluminium or brass. Get the centre spacing right against the shutter width — a handle that is too short makes a tall wardrobe door look stubby.

materials.name: Profile handle
materials.blurb: Continuous aluminium profile fixed along the shutter edge
materials.description: Runs the full width of the shutter and reads as a line rather than an object. Keeps a long kitchen run visually calm and is far more forgiving than push-to-open on site tolerances.

materials.name: G-profile handle
materials.blurb: Recessed G-section that gives a grip without projecting
materials.description: The G-shape is fixed behind the shutter top edge so nothing sticks out into the room. The default handle-less detail for kitchens where push-to-open is judged too fussy.

materials.name: Edge profile handle
materials.blurb: L or J section fitted to the shutter edge itself
materials.description: The profile becomes the shutter edge, so the joinery reads as a single plane. Best with matte finishes; a gloss edge profile shows every knock.

materials.name: Knob
materials.blurb: Single-point pull for small shutters and drawers
materials.description: One screw, endless variety — ceramic, brass, wood, leather-wrapped. Right for small drawers and traditional schemes; wrong for anything heavy that needs two hands.

materials.name: Leather handle
materials.blurb: Stitched leather strap — warm, tactile, hospitality-grade
materials.description: A leather pull softens a hard scheme and ages well if it is real hide rather than PU. Popular on bedroom joinery and boutique hospitality work.

materials.name: Brass handle
materials.blurb: Solid brass in antique, satin or unlacquered finishes
materials.description: Real brass has weight in the hand that plated steel never fakes. Unlacquered brass will patina — a feature if the client is told, a complaint if they are not.

materials.name: Aluminium handle
materials.blurb: Light, corrosion-free and the cheapest clean-looking option
materials.description: Extruded and anodised aluminium keeps cost down without looking cheap, and it will not rust in a coastal flat. Softer than steel, so it dents if treated roughly.

materials.name: Stainless steel handle
materials.blurb: SS 304 pulls that survive kitchens and coastal air
materials.description: The dependable specification: 304-grade stainless resists kitchen grease, cleaning chemicals and salt air. Insist on 304 rather than 202, which will spot within a year near the sea.

materials.name: Invisible / recessed handle
materials.blurb: Machined pocket in the shutter — nothing added at all
materials.description: A finger recess routed into the shutter face or edge, so the joinery has no hardware on it whatsoever. Requires CNC work and a finish that will survive being touched in one spot forever.

specs.Finish: Must be durable at the touch point
